Classical image (very brief): Earth square, elephant, linga–yoni, coiled serpent asleep at base
Jung’s psychological meaning: Ordinaryegolife, rooted in bodily existence, duties, family, “this-world” reality; the “root support” of personal consciousness.
Kundalinī’s status / movement: Kundalinī isasleep; the gods (impersonal factors) are dormant, so the ego seems to be the only active principle.

Jung’s psychological meaning: Realm ofinstinctual desire, fantasy, and unconscious contents, like a baptismal basin or womb of rebirth where one is immersed in psychic material beyond the day‑ego.
Kundalinī’s status / movement: Awakening begins as a compulsion or “divine urge” (neurosis, fear, fascination) thatforcesone deeper, like the dragon in Poliphilo that blocks retreat.

Classical image (very brief): Fire, solar, city of jewels, ram
Jung’s psychological meaning: Center ofemotional fire, will, power, and affect; here libido becomes more intense, aggressive, and differentiated—linked to heroic, “Herculean” labors and conflicts of power.
Kundalinī’s status / movement: Kundalinī’s ascent into fire: psychic energy is no longer just fantasy‑water but becomesburningpassion and conflict that can transform or consume.

Classical image (very brief): Heart, air, double triangle, antelope, inner sound
Jung’s psychological meaning: Emergence of atruly impersonal standpoint(the “heart” as a center beyond purely personal emotion), where the individual can relate to symbols and archetypes without total identification; beginning of real Self‑relation.
Kundalinī’s status / movement: Kundalinī here marks a shift from personal totranspersonal; visions take on objective, symbolic character rather than being read as mere personal symptoms.

Jung’s psychological meaning: Level ofsymbolic speech, logos, and subtle thought, where inner experiences are given pure form (myth, philosophy, spiritual language) rather than concrete imagery.
Kundalinī’s status / movement: The rising energy is expressed inword and understanding; psyche becomes capable of transparent, symbolic articulation of archetypal contents.

Jung’s psychological meaning: Center ofvision, insight, and directive awareness—a unifying standpoint where opposites are held together and the ego is relativized by a higher organizing principle (analogous to the Self).
Kundalinī’s status / movement: Kundalinī at ājñā corresponds to anorganized relationto the unconscious: the “world of the gods” is experienced as real, but the ego does not claim to be that world.
